rules.title: テスト本体にArrangeを置かない
rules.sourceSection: テスト構造 > Arrangeの分離方法

question.instructions: Classify whether the test file follows the project rule that meaningful Arrange setup must be kept outside individual test bodies. Evaluate the whole file.

criteria.violation: One or more test bodies perform meaningful Arrange work that should be prepared outside the test body. This includes constructing test data, creating initial state, setting up mocks or spies, or performing initial rendering. Values received from test.each parameters are allowed. Assigning the result of the operation under test is Act, not Arrange.
criteria.compliant: Test bodies focus on Act and Assert. Meaningful Arrange work is prepared in the surrounding describe scope, beforeEach, or test.each case data.
criteria.not_applicable: The tests require no meaningful Arrange setup, so there is no relevant setup that should be moved outside a test body.
criteria.insufficient_context: The available source does not provide enough information to distinguish setup from the behavior being exercised.

rules.title: beforeEachは事前準備だけを行う
rules.sourceSection: テスト構造 > Arrangeの分離方法

question.instructions: Classify whether every beforeEach in the test file follows the project rule that beforeEach performs Arrange only and does not execute the behavior under test.

criteria.violation: A beforeEach executes an operation, user action, or behavior whose result is subsequently verified by a test. The behavior being tested should instead be executed in the individual test body.
criteria.compliant: beforeEach blocks only prepare initial state, test data, mocks, spies, dependencies, or initial rendering. The behavior under test is executed inside each test.
criteria.insufficient_context: A beforeEach calls helpers whose role cannot be determined from the available source, so it is unclear whether they perform setup or the behavior under test.

rules.title: DOMテストは利用者から観測できる契約を優先する
rules.sourceSection: テスト構造 > 基本原則

question.instructions: Classify whether DOM-oriented tests in this file primarily verify user-observable contracts rather than incidental implementation details.

criteria.violation: One or more DOM tests primarily assert incidental implementation details even though the intended behavior could reasonably be verified through roles, accessible names, visible content, or observable results after user interaction.
criteria.compliant: DOM tests primarily verify behavior through roles, accessible names, visible content, or results observable after user interaction.
criteria.not_applicable: The file contains no DOM-oriented tests.
criteria.insufficient_context: The available source is insufficient to determine whether an asserted detail is an intended user-facing contract or merely an implementation detail.

rules.title: 同じ期待動作の入力違いはtest.eachで表現する

question.instructions: Classify whether repeated test cases in this file follow the project rule that cases verifying the same expected behavior with different inputs should use test.each.

criteria.violation: Two or more separate test cases repeat substantially the same Act and Assert structure and differ mainly in input values or expected values, so they should be represented with test.each.
criteria.compliant: Repeated cases are already represented with test.each, or separate tests verify materially different behaviors that deserve independent test cases.
criteria.not_applicable: The file has no repeated test cases representing the same behavior with different inputs or expected values.
criteria.insufficient_context: The available source does not make it possible to determine whether superficially similar tests represent the same expected behavior.
